# coder CLI

Delegate a coding task to the best available engine and steer it while it runs.

- [task](task.md): run, follow and steer coding tasks
- [flow](flow.md): orchestrate many coder tasks from one TypeScript file
- [agent](agent.md): define and run agents
- [credentials](credentials.md): engine credentials: subscriptions and API keys
- [server](server.md): self-host Coder: the server, its dashboard and sign-in
- [runner](runner.md): run your server's tasks on this machine
- [auth](auth.md): sign in to Coder and manage saved server sessions
- [model](model.md): manage models: built-ins, aliases, custom endpoints
- [connection](connection.md): platform accounts, API keys and MCP servers tasks use

## `review [--base <base>] [--head <head>] [--pr <pr>] [--since <since>] [--path <path>] [--exclude <exclude>] [--post] [--md] [--engine <engine>] [--model <model>] [--effort <effort>] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

review changed code with a built-in flow

Review changed code with a read-only agent. Every reported finding is checked
against the repository. Runs the built-in `review` flow. A local review covers
everything since the merge-base with the origin default branch, including
uncommitted and untracked files. Changed submodules are reviewed file by file.
PR reviews can post deduplicated inline comments.

Related: `coder flow watch`, `coder docs review`.

- `--base <base>` local comparison base (default: merge-base with origin default)
- `--head <head>` review commits through this ref only (default: the working tree)
- `--pr <pr>` review a pull request by number (origin repo) or URL; GitHub via gh for now
- `--since <since>` keep only PR files and hunks changed since this commit
- `--path <path>` review only this path, relative to cwd (repeatable)
- `--exclude <exclude>` leave this path out, relative to cwd (repeatable)
- `--post` post deduplicated inline comments and sticky PR summary
- `--md` markdown output (the default)
- `--engine <engine>` codex, claude, or custom
- `--model <model>` model for the review task
- `--effort <effort>` reasoning effort and review depth (default: medium depth)
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

```sh
coder review  # review the branch plus uncommitted work
coder review --base main  # review everything since main locally
coder review --path src --exclude src/gen  # review src without generated code
coder review --pr 42 --post  # review and post to pull request 42
```

## `config [action] [key] [value] [--workspace] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

read or write config

Read or write configuration. `list` prints the effective config; get/set/unset
target a dotted key (e.g. engines.codex.model). Writes go to ~/.coder/config.json.

- `<action>` list, get, set or unset
- `<key>` a dotted key, such as engines.codex.model
- `<value>` with set: the value; JSON, or a comma list
- `--workspace` target <repo>/.coder/config.json instead of the user file
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

```sh
coder config list  # print the effective config
coder config set chain codex,claude  # set the engine fallback chain
coder config get engines.codex.model  # read one value
```

## `setup-host [hosts] [--json] [--cwd <cwd>]`

check engines and install the host plugin or skill

Set up coder in your host: check engines and auth, seed the config, and
install the host plugin/skill for the named host(s). Claude Code gets its
marketplace plugin; "agents" installs a skill into ~/.agents/skills for
every host that reads the Agent Skills standard dir (Codex, Pi, OpenCode,
...). Codex and Cursor also get the MCP server; the Claude plugin includes it.
With no host, checks, seeds and registers available Codex and Cursor hosts.

To add the MCP server by hand: claude mcp add coder -- coder mcp, codex mcp
add coder -- coder mcp, or for Cursor "coder": { "command": "coder", "args":
["mcp"] } under mcpServers in ~/.cursor/mcp.json. Restart running sessions after.

- `<hosts>` claude, agents, codex, cursor (one or more)
- `--json` JSON output
- `--cwd <cwd>` workspace directory; default current

```sh
coder setup-host claude  # install the Claude Code plugin
coder setup-host agents  # install the shared skill and register MCP with available Codex
coder setup-host codex cursor  # install the skill and register MCP with both hosts
```

## `docs [topic] [--claude] [--json]`

print bundled documentation (for agents to read)

Print bundled documentation. With no topic, list the available topics; with a
topic, print that doc's raw markdown to stdout (unstyled, for an agent to
consume). Topics with sub-pages list them as `<topic>/<page>` (also accepted as
`<topic>-<page>`). `coder docs skill` prints the host skill so an engine can
load it once per session (--claude for the Claude Code flavor).

- `<topic>` the doc to print (default: list the topics)
- `--claude` with the skill topic: print the Claude Code flavor
- `--json` JSON output

```sh
coder docs  # list the available topics
coder docs flows  # print the Flows doc
coder docs review  # print the Review doc
```

## `upgrade [--cli-only] [--plugins-only] [--codex] [--claude] [--pm <pm>]`

update the CLI and host plugins

Update the coder CLI through whichever package manager installed it, then refresh
the host plugins to match.

- `--cli-only` update just the CLI
- `--plugins-only` refresh just the host plugins
- `--codex` limit the refresh to the Agent Skills copy (Codex, Pi, ...)
- `--claude` limit the refresh to the Claude Code plugin
- `--pm <pm>` force a package manager instead of auto-detecting

## `mcp`

serve Coder's commands as MCP tools over stdio

Serve Coder's commands as MCP tools over stdio, so a harness can run them.

Commands return their JSON payloads and next steps. Load guides with load_skill;
blocking commands keep their CLI flags and behavior, subject to the client's tool timeout.

```sh
claude mcp add coder -- coder mcp  # run Coder from Claude Code
```
